h1: Palomar Labs — AI & SaaS Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product, captured at 1920x1422 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product — glass panels, looping video, React and Tailwind CSS and 240ms transitions.
about: Palomar Labs gives an AI or SaaS product a finished first screen and the numbers that produced it. The colour scheme is white #F5F3EF underneath and deep green #2D3A2E for the type, and the page is set in Montserrat. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 1920x1422 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Motion is confined to 240ms transitions, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) and a looping video bed. Keep it open while you write: the 7,574-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: The nav is deliberately thin
layout.body: Navigation is a single row with no second level under it. A mobile overlay takes over below the tablet breakpoint. The bar sits over the 1920x1422 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it. Give the wordmark no more room than its type needs.

layout.title: The sizes are in the brief, not in a scale
layout.body: The brief names the numbers: 20px spacing steps, 240ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) easing. That is why the composition holds together, because there is no invented spacing step between the type and the frame. The list is short enough that a reviewer can check it element by element.

layout.title: Numbered lines do the work
layout.body: The features are set as a list in Montserrat rather than as a wall of cards. Items share one size and one marker, which keeps a long list scannable.

layout.title: A navigation bar that gets out of the way
layout.body: The mobile menu is part of the brief, so the collapsed state is designed rather than improvised. Keep the row to one line.

motion.title: Pointer states, nothing more
motion.body: Feedback is limited to hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card, which is what keeps a dense first screen from feeling busy. Because the states are simple, they port into any component system. Do not animate layout on hover.

motion.title: Timing kept in the brief
motion.body: Every state change in the specification has a duration attached: transitions settle around 240ms using cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). Nothing is left at the browser default, which is why the page feels authored rather than animated. Short timings are why the page reads as authored; a slow default would undo the composition.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over white #F5F3EF, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.

editorial.title: The numbers behind the landing page
editorial.body: When a rebuild drifts, the spacing goes first. Palomar Labs avoids that by publishing 20px spacing steps, 240ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) easing with the composition. Nothing in this landing page depends on a default.

editorial.title: What moves in Palomar Labs
editorial.body: A preset animation library would give you more movement than this. The brief asks for less: 240ms transitions, a 6.7s media loop and hover and press states, and nothing decorative on top. Nothing animates for its own sake in this landing page.

editorial.title: Why this composition works for SaaS
editorial.body: Suppose your media is louder than your copy. That is the case this composition is built for. The media is a 6.7s 1920x1422 loop. The frame stays quiet and 20px spacing steps and 240ms transitions keep the reader on the text. Palomar Labs states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

faq.question: How long is the prompt behind Palomar Labs?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 1920x1422, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: How much of Palomar Labs depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Palomar Labs was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Where did the Palomar Labs design come from?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 1920x1422.
